scope: Direct PostgreSQL text columns as B-tree keys with an explicitly resolved stock C collation, INCLUDE columns, and row NULL predicates.
rules: An explicitly selected stock pg_catalog.C text key resolves to byte ordering over UTF-8 and the stock text_ops operator class. The default text operator class and an explicit pg_catalog.text_ops denote the same checked role.

The exact collation is recorded on each key occurrence, independently of preceding keys, repeated text keys, null positioning, and sort direction. A numeric or Boolean key cannot supply a text collation.
A text field used only by INCLUDE or a row NULL test preserves its type and exact physical slot. The included value and a NULL predicate use no key collation.
A completed B-tree carrying text operands retains the same sparse physical projection used for numeric and Boolean operands. The declaring heading and table default collation remain external inputs.

Unresolved inherited default collations, unqualified collation or operator-class selectors, and other text operator classes are separate obligations in the full language inventory. Keep their admission failures explicit until their own binding rules are implemented.
sql: Use an absolute table coordinate and a quoted identifier for every selected physical occurrence.

For every text key print COLLATE pg_catalog."C" and the resolved pg_catalog.text_ops before ordering. Print covering text fields as column identifiers and row NULL tests as the corresponding grouped predicates.
observations: Compare absolute owner, sparse operand types and slots, per-key collation and operator class, stable result heading, key order and exact INCLUDE position.
Compare commands, raw SQLSTATEs, native pg_index arrays, qualified collation and operator-class identities, ordered typed values, row NULL predicates, and the outcomes of duplicate and NULL writes.
Use UTF-8 byte-distinct values, including case pairs, accent pairs, composed and decomposed Unicode, repeated rows and SQL NULL. Compare C ordering against an independent byte comparator.
negative: A direct text key lacks a resolved collation
A direct non-text key carries a text collation
An analyzed text key specifies another stock collation
An analyzed text key specifies another stock operator class
An analyzed numeric key specifies the text collation
faults: Omit the C collation when rendering against a text column declared with a different default
Use the same key collation for a different physical slot
Ignore a native collation coordinate when comparing
trust: The pinned built-in PostgreSQL catalog and native UTF-8 settings
Exact checked PHP construction rules, independent B-tree observable definition, and separate native witness
